# ENDOPHTHALMITIS

Endophthalmitis is a medical emergency and presents with eye pain and visual loss. It may be associated with gram positive or gram-negative bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, or with fungi.

Consult ophthalmology immediately. The ophthalmologist will obtain an aqueous or vitreous fluid sample for gram stain and culture and begin intravitreal antimicrobials.

## Fungal endophthalmitis

Fungal endophthalmitis is rarely diagnosed in temperate climates and treatment is complicated. Ophthalmology and Infectious Diseases involvement is essential.

- References: Mandell chapter: Endophthalmitis

Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Treatment with intravitreal antimicrobials

Consult Infectious Diseases and Ophthalmology

## Outpatient

### Treatment with intravitreal antimicrobials

Vancomycin 1 mg/0.1 mL intravitreal injection STAT ($) [R] < AND > ceftazidime 2.25 mg/0.1 mL intravitreal injection STAT ($$) [M]
< OR >
Vancomycin 1 mg/0.1 mL intravitreal injection STAT ($) [R] < AND > amikacin 0.4 mg/0.1 mL intravitreal injection STAT ($$) [M]

### Fungal endophthalmitis

Fungal endophthalmitis is rarely diagnosed in temperate climates and treatment is complicated. Ophthalmology and Infectious Diseases involvement is essential.

Amphotericin B 5mcg/0.1mL intravitreal injection STAT ($$$) [R,O]
< OR >
Voriconazole 100 mcg/0.1mL intravitreal injection STAT ($$$$) [R,H,DI]
